subject: Catalyst integration preflight and deterministic test matrix
messages:
From: Ian Cole <ian.cole@catalyst.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: partners@catalyst.io
Date: 2027-03-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood / Catalyst preflight: kick-off and data points

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking this. Catalyst wants to move the Redwood integration from discovery to a short technical preflight this quarter. Our goal is to validate the reference path end-to-end (auth, inference latency under 4xx tokens, deterministic batching behavior) and confirm the deployment pattern for our customers (private deployments + hosted fallbacks).

Top asks from our side to structure the preflight:
- Mutual action plan (timeline, owners)
- A deterministic test matrix (what we run for pass/fail)
- Network/egress and TLS expectations for private runs
- Where we should drop sample telemetry/logs for you to consume

Can you share a preflight matrix and a reference architecture PDF we can circulate internally? Also propose 30–45 minute windows for a technical alignment call this week.

Thanks,
Ian Cole
Head of Integrations, Catalyst Systems
ian.cole@catalyst.io
+1 415-555-0173

Attachment: (none in this message)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ian Cole <ian.cole@catalyst.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood / Catalyst preflight: kick-off and data points

Ian —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached a concise preflight matrix (redwood-catalyst-preflight-matrix.xlsx) and a short reference design (redwood-reference-design-v1.pdf) that lays out two deployment patterns: 1) Private (VPC) with private control plane, and 2) Hybrid (Dedicated pool + hosted fallback).

Quick notes:
- Owners: Vanessa (partner coordination), Marissa (QA/runbooks), Karthik (deployment patterns), Sergio (runtime/ops).
- Suggested timeline: 2-week preflight (week 1: environment & connectivity; week 2: smoke tests + perf/regen checks).
- Deterministic tests in the matrix include: auth handshakes, prefix-cache consistency, KV cache warmup, 1k-token generation latency profile at batch sizes 1/4/8, and quality regression on a 20-prompt suite.

Can you confirm Catalyst will provide a small representative dataset and a short-lived API key for the smoke tests? If you can share two 10-minute windows for a shared call (our SAs are western US based), I'll lock something in.

Thanks — attaching files.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Attachments:
- redwood-catalyst-preflight-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 23KB)
- redwood-reference-design-v1.pdf (pdf, 312KB)
From: Michael Tran <michael.tran@catalyst.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ian Cole <ian.cole@catalyst.io>
Date: 2027-03-21T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood / Catalyst preflight: kick-off and data points

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. We downloaded the matrix and design; looks well scoped. A few clarifications:
1) API key: we can generate a scoped, short-lived key for your smoke environment (valid 72 hours).
2) Dataset: we'll provide a 100-prompt sample (anonymized) and a small eval set (20 prompts + expected outputs) for the regression checks.
3) Network: for our private customers we can open destination egress to 52.34.120.0/22 and provide cert thumbprints for mTLS.

I've attached a small tarball with sample logs and a JSON snippet showing the request/response headers we typically emit (catalyst-sample-logs.tar.gz). If Sergio's team needs anything in a different format let me know.

We can do 3/21 4:00–4:45pm PDT or 3/22 9:00–9:45am PDT for a tech call — which works for you?

Best,
Michael Tran
Integration Lead, Catalyst Systems
michael.tran@catalyst.io

Attachment: catalyst-sample-logs.tar.gz (log bundle, ~1.8MB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Tran <michael.tran@catalyst.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood / Catalyst preflight: kick-off and data points

Michael / all —

Quick technical ack and a few asks so the smoke run is smooth:
- Auth: short-lived API key is fine; please include x-catalyst-request-id in headers for tracing.
- TLS/mTLS: we'll accept cert thumbprint verification on the control plane; for private deployments we'll validate client certs during the smoke handshake.
- Networking: the egress block above works; we'll also need FQDNs for hosted fallbacks (we'll provide a small allowlist).
- Perf: when you send the sample JSON, include tokenization characteristics (avg tokens per prompt) so we can set the KV cache warmup properly.

I attached a short smoke-test runbook (smoke-test-runbook.md) that our SREs will follow. Key checkpoints: connectivity, auth, baseline latency (p50/p95), deterministic prefix check, and regression comparison on the 20-prompt suite. For regression we expect Catalyst to provide "expected" outputs; we'll run a normalized diff and flag any variance above a 5% token-level divergence.

If you can drop the sample dataset to the Drive link Vanessa shared and confirm the temp API key by EOD we can run the smoke tomorrow morning (3/22 9:00am PDT).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: smoke-test-runbook.md (markdown, 6KB)

Michael / Ian —

Great — thanks for the artifacts. Confirming:
- Catalyst will upload the 100-prompt sample + 20-prompt eval to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxy-example-abc123
- Catalyst will create a scoped API key valid for 72 hours and share the key via the HubSpot secure note (JIRA CATALYST-47 adds the secure token link).
- Tech call scheduled: 2027-03-22 09:00–09:45 PDT (meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-meet). Attendees: Vanessa, Sergio, Marissa, Karthik, Ian, Michael.

Next steps (owners):
- Catalyst: upload dataset + temp API key (Ian/Michael) — owner: Ian — due: 2027-03-21 17:00 PDT (slipped but still OK for tomorrow).
- Redwood SRE: run smoke test per runbook — owner: Sergio — due: 2027-03-22 11:30 PDT (deliverable: smoke run results + perf snapshots).
- Redwood QA: run regression diff against expected outputs — owner: Marissa — due: 2027-03-22 14:00 PDT.

I'll keep this thread for artifacts and results. If the smoke passes we'll produce a short technical sign-off and a follow-up plan for a limited pilot.

Thanks everyone — see you on the call.

--
